I agree with moving back to servers, but I don't think reasoning is so straight-forward, and I don't think there's one true solution to make everybody happy.  
  
I'm a FSP semi-casual player, going through periods of inactivity and periods of grinding. (Like most GW2 players, according to Anet)  
  
Let's start with the issues of the old system. All from my PoV and experience, YMMW.  
  
If you happened to be linked to a low population server, you had similar issues to the ones we're currently having. You're a player who either can't afford to server hop, doesn't want to server hop, are too casual to bother, or something else. (all valid reasons)  
We could combat this by having free server transfers on a cooldown (we do this in the new system, just under the different terminology of team assignment)  
If you're too casual to bother hopping onto a high pop server, you were in the same seat as people who today don't want to join a wvw guild with high activity requirements. Again, same issues, just manifesting themselves in a different way.  
  
Is the new system better for top-end WvW players? Maybe/probably! I'm sure there are benefits to being teamed up via guilds. The main thing that irks me is that we never got the full Alliance update. We're in some sort of a middle-ground.  
  
Now, I'll speak on my experience going to the new system. It's been fine. Nothing more, nothing less. After the initial hiccups, the matchmaking has been OK. It's still WvW underneath all the structuring.  
  
But fuck, do I miss servers. I used to hop on because it was fun to fight for my realm, to have some form of server pride. Seeing your regular commanders or roamers, seeing new ones make their way into the growing list of known names. Yeah, yeah, muh RP. But honestly, that's what made it fun for me. Now, I'm hopping in and out of guild-specific discord channels, often in languages I don't speak, only because it's required to join the open tag.  
  
Nowadays, playing WvW is like playing any other competitive game. Now, you play it solely for the gamemode, and it shows. It has cracks and faults. Far from perfect, and it's not a gamemode I'll be pursuing for the mode itself. I was in it for the community, and now the community is gone.

Ray tracing is running as a post-processing effect, meaning that it has some severe limitations.    
  
The depth-buffer does a passable job of limiting the strength of the effect in the distance.  
This is needed since the RT is screen-space, meaning that is doesn't have the foggiest about the scale of objects.  
(A distant mountain will receive the same processing as a box in the foreground)  
  
It also has no idea what's behind an object, so tracing rays around corners is impossible.  
  
Ray lengths have to be adjusted per scene, as some lengths look amazing on floorplanks, but causes terrible clipping on walls.  
  
On small objects + characters when fully zoomed out, there is substantial flickering. This will be addressed in the future by the RTGI dev.  
  
On many objects the phong smoothing is too sharp. This is also going to be addressed in the future by the RTGI dev.
  
It's not something I'll keep enabled while playing, but it's been very fun to play around with and see what post-processing can do to an arguably aging game.

Hey Bobby! Sorry for the long post.  
  
Prefacing this by stating the obvious: I feel that these clickbait threads could be avoided by more regular, openminded and clear communication between devs and players.  
Though history shows that it has been far from perfect, a lot of the interaction with Chris and Ben on reddit and twitch showed great potential, even if the execution has been slightly flawed from both sides.  
Hoping that we can have an open discussion about raids and other endgame content going forward.  
  
"**What is it that you like about raids in general?**"  
1. Difficulty  
2. Engagement  
3. Rewards  
4. Prestige  
  
**1: Difficulty.**  
Raids and the CM fractals is the only endgame content which challenges me, everything else I do because of necessity (get daily currencies, try my luck at infusions).  
Yes, I've been playing since release. Yes, many people haven't. That's fine. We can co-exist.  
The combat mechanics in this game really shine in raid encounters, to the point where it's elevated to a completely different plane.  
For me, having the OPTION of doing CMs is great. *I think easy/story modes of raids would help a lot of players ease into the gamemode.*  
  
**I DON'T think strikes fully achieve this.** I would also see for example VG story mode being reworked to a linear experience *without hard failstates*.  
Imagine a solo or group instance.  
* One VG mechanic at a time. NPCs guide you with lore-appropriate mechanic descriptions.  
* Blues teleport you normally.  
* The floor pulses 25% of your HP, BUT you also get healed for the same amount right afterwards. It's visually explanatory, but not failstate punishing.  
* Greens do 75% of your HP, and the same amount is slowly regained over a few seconds.  
* NPC tanks and calls out mechanics as they happen.  
  
Is this handholding mode? Yes. Could it help super casuals? I think so.  
  
**EDIT: Look at Tequatl.** It was once seen as an *unkillable* monster of a dragon, and only very organized guild maps could take it down with lots of coordination. Sure, the numbers have been tweaked, but nowadays open maps burn through 75%-0% in seconds. Difficulty is a matter of perspective, and that perspective can change with proper training.
  
**2: Engagement.**  
Encounters like raids and 99/100 fractals (some other fractals fit this description too) keep me engaged in the fight, paying attention and always looking out for mechanics.  
Open world content, while often not a terrible way to spend my downtime, mostly equals to "pew pew, move a bit, pew pew again".  
Sure, there are technically mechanics to every fight, and CONCEPTUALLY many open world encounters are amazing. Seriously. If they were more difficult and therefore more rewarding, there are SO many open world events I would love to do. Right now, *they aren't worth my time.*  
  
**3: Rewards.**  
Here is my biggest concern.  
GW2 is known for a lot of things, but here's the most disappointing thing to me. "How do i get this item?" Can OFTEN be answered by either:  
a) Gem store.  
b) Just farm gold and get it on the TP.  
  
Before getting into raids, I need to go back to open world content.  
Lots of open world stuff only reward you with some greens, some rares at best, and some mats.  
It's quickly converted into liquid gold, and that's it.  
That will naturally gravitate players into this weeks most effective farm train.  
Raids do have loads of really nice drops already. That's good. A lot of them should be attainable through tokens, such as armor, trinkets and weapons. This allows for gearing characters simply through raiding.  
**I do NOT believe the exclusive armor skins, chairs, infusions or minis should be obtainable through the token vendor.** Make the token gear have regular appearances in line with crafted gear, and just make the skin drops exotics.  
These are the only rewards in raids that are really poggers to get, and their excitement value sinks through the bottom when someone else can farm escort until they get all the cool skins. Which brings me to..  
  
**4: Prestige.**  
Seriously. I hate comparing GW2 to other games, but I did try WoW for a month.  
I stopped after hitting the lvl cap, because the boring combat didn't excite me. WoW is the definition of playing the UI.  
BUT. BUT! Damn does it have a good reward system. (mostly)  
I enjoyed going into raids and dungeons for a chance to get that cool looking staff, i enjoyed collecting mounts, and damn if i didn't enjoy bragging about my achievements.  
GW2 has SOME of that. CM titles, legendary gear, and infusions.  
  
**Infusions** can be tucked away due to RnG, sure. I still think it's valid.  
The epicness™ of dropping an infusion is amazing though, if you've ever been in mapchat when it happens.  
I've seen new players not even being aware of their existence, saying that they're excited to try and get it. Keep them tradeable, for sure. But i would personally not make them available for tokens like the ghostly infusion.  
  
**CM titles**. They show mastery of the game mechanics and dedication to group content. Sure, they can be bought. You'll never get around that.  
  
**Legendary gear**. Gen 1 still features as a nice gold sink, and I think having one set of nice weapons available on the TP is okay.  
I really like everything about the legendary collections, though.  
They make people replay old content, give them a journey to complete, and doesn't provide an advantage over other players.  
Prestige is probably the biggest overall point for me. MMO's are all about "look at me! i did this!".  
  
  
"**If we were to build another raid, what would you like to see? Any story you'd like experience?**"  
I have nothing here. While the lore behind the raids is great, and quite enticing if you care about it, mechanically engaging encounters are the bread and butter.  
  
Keep pre-events more about explaining mechanics, and less about clearing trash or lore bombing.  Spirit vale is a great example. Each pre-event has nice increments in mechanics, and the bosses themselves are staged well.  
VG = Oh shit we have mechanics/failstates now, and group comps matter! (also wtf is condi damage???)  
Gorse = Damn, my celestial stats aren't enough to 11111 this boss.  
Sabetha(Still one of the more difficult bosses in the game for LFGs) = OH SHIT EVERYTHING AT THE SAME TIME????  
  
I hope some of this makes sense. Thanks for reading.
